 Bayern Munich v Arsenal preview: Key stats and player info 
 By Tom McCoy BBC Sport journalist Published 7 hours ago 
 The champions of Germany and England meet in an eagerly anticipated fixture which, but for Bayern's Munich semi-final defeat by Paris St-Germain, would have been last season's final. 
 The hosts' expansive, high-risk approach contrasts with Arsenal's more measured and disciplined style.
 The Bavarians, unbeaten at home in the group stage or league phase of European competition for 13 years, have scored 23 goals in their four home games this season.
 However, they have kept just three clean sheets in 10 matches this term and conceded three times in last week's draw with Viking, a result boss Vincent Kompany blamed on individual mistakes.
 Bayern will need to be almost error-free against an Arsenal side with a similarly outstanding record at this stage.
 The Gunners have won 14 consecutive Champions League games in the opening phase of the competition, including a 3-1 victory when the sides met at the Emirates last November.
 Harry Kane drew a blank that night, but the former Tottenham star has an excellent record against his old north London rivals and is looking to score in a 10th consecutive Champions League game.
 Did you know? 
 Bayern are unbeaten in 39 Champions League group stage or league phase matches at home (W37, D2) since losing 3-2 to Manchester City in December 2013.
 Bayern have scored in 23 consecutive European games, with their past eight outings producing a total of 44 goals, an average of 5.5 per game.
 Image source, Getty Images Key Bayern Munich players - Harry Kane 
 England's captain already has records galore to his name but there is another in his sights. He has scored in nine consecutive Champions League games, two short of the record set by Cristiano Ronaldo from 2017 to 2018.
 Kane has nine goals already this season and 15 for club and country.
 His outstanding form has made him a leading contender to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday and Bayern are understandably keen to tie him down to a new contract. 
 Last week, it was reported a new deal, running until 2029, had been agreed in principle.
 The former Spurs player has netted 15 times in 22 games against Arsenal.
 Bayern Munich team news 
 Winger Michael Olise is suspended, with Serge Gnabry or Lennart Karl in contention to replace him.
 Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer missed out at the weekend with a foot injury, while defender Kim Min-jae may also need to be assessed. Forward Jamal Musiala is sidelined by a thigh issue.
